title: Continuity
summary: Continuity formalizes preservation of nearness or open-set structure under a map.

context.note: Framework is named textually in this seed release; full recursive first-principles closure remains future work.

assumptions.text: Topological spaces X and Y and a function f:X→Y are specified.

content.plain: A continuous map does not tear apart the chosen topology: inverse images of observable open regions remain open.
content.exact: f:X→Y is continuous iff for every open V⊆Y, f^{-1}(V) is open in X. In metric spaces this is equivalent to the ε-δ definition.
content.example: f(x)=x^2 is continuous on R with its usual topology.
content.caveat: Continuity is relative to the chosen topologies; a function can be continuous under one topology and not another.

relations.note: Many stability notions are formulated using neighborhoods or metrics.
Discrete spaces make every function out of them continuous.
